title: Sahara Desert: Climate and Size
text: The Sahara Desert covers approximately 9.2 million square kilometers across North Africa, making it the world's largest hot desert. It spans from the Atlantic Ocean on the west to the Red Sea on the east, and from the Mediterranean Sea in the north to the Sahel in the south. Average annual rainfall in most of the Sahara is less than 25 mm, and large areas receive less than 5 mm per year. Surface temperatures can exceed 70°C. Despite its reputation, the Sahara has experienced wet periods, called the Green Sahara, approximately 11,000–5,000 years ago when monsoon rains supported grasslands, lakes, and human settlements.
